headline: Variants that compile to class toggles fold to a string concat, so `next-yak-9.7` leads; the case also splits Panda in two — its precompiled `cva` recipe joins the fast cluster while its per-prop `css()` fn is the slowest lane by far.

microbench.why: The variant props compile to class toggles, so `next-yak-9.7` inlines them to a string concat and folds the wrapper away, leading at 0.645 ms/1k. The way each library expresses variants decides the rest: `panda`'s `css()` fn re-serializes every variant per element, dumping 13.0 ms into component self-time (13.2 ms/1k, the slowest lane), while its `cva` recipe precompiles the variants and joins the fast cluster at 0.810 ms/1k — a 16× swing inside one library. `styled-components` (1.61 ms/1k) and `emotion` (2.92 ms/1k) still hash per variant.

autocannon.why: The folded toggle lane serves the most requests because each request emits static classes; `panda`'s css-fn re-serializes variants per request and collapses to 76 req/s, 21× fewer than the folded lane.

attribution.why: The extracted lanes render in ~0.6-0.8 ms with a near-zero library slice (`next-yak-css-9.7` 0.106 ms, `next-yak-9.7` 0.127 ms after the toggle fold). `panda`'s css-fn is the outlier by an order of magnitude — 13.0 ms of component self-time re-serializing variants — where its recipe lane sits at 0.863 ms. `emotion` (lib 1.43 ms) and `styled-components` (lib 0.648 ms) carry variant hashing.

hydrate.why: Extracted lanes hydrate as pure JS; the folded styled lane leads at 41.3 ms. The runtime libraries inject on hydrate — `panda` 97.6 ms, `styled-components` 98.0 ms — ~2.4× the folded floor.

inp.why: With static variants, changing one button re-renders one element; nearly every lane does it in ~7-7.7 ms within the interaction spread, and even `styled-components` joins because a static variant regenerates no class on interaction. `panda`'s css-fn stays back at 44.8 ms, still serializing on the re-render.

mount.why: Extracted lanes mount at ~68-73 ms; the runtime libraries add first-inject (`styled-components` 92.6 ms, `emotion` 96.5 ms, `panda` 125 ms).

renderTiming.why: One style recalc for every approach — parity; the styleMs spread (0.122-0.430 ms) is sub-millisecond and the higher figures (`cnfast`, `emotion`) come from their injected sheet, not extra recalcs.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships smallest (3.39 kB gz), the styled toggle lane 4.47 kB, `panda`'s recipe 5.75 kB. The utility and runtime lanes are 3.3-3.8× larger (`tailwind-merge` 15.0 kB, `emotion` 16.2 kB, `styled-components` 16.8 kB).

nsweep.why: At 4000 buttons the folded toggle lane stays flat with react-dom (2.11 ms); `panda`'s css-fn compounds its per-variant serialize to 51.9 ms, the steepest curve, while its recipe lane stays at 2.60 ms.

crossCase: `btn-variant` and `product-grid` above are the two class-toggle cases: both express variants as `$prop` toggles that next-yak inlines to a string concat and folds, which is why the styled and css-prop lanes sit at the static-class floor in each. `btn-variant` also isolates the API choice within Panda — the `cva` recipe precompiles variants (fast) where the inline `css()` fn re-serializes them per element (slowest lane in the case).
